//AuroraGlow: The aurora's mood, the second half of the aurora DECISION (Documentation/Research/HarshWilds/events_sky.md section 5): while hw_stat_aurora runs (armed by Tgr_HW_AuroraRoll.json) and the player is OUTSIDE at night under an open sky, it writes vanilla Morale (4a27fb5da9326b545a5ef73f2b80316e, the vanilla mood stat, 'Shows your general mood') a small step every tick. RepeatOptions 0 (Repeat) with OncePerTick and no cooldown, so it fires on every eligible tick (the Tgr_HW_PlagueSwarm and Tgr_HW_DrySpellHold shape, measured working). ALL GATES ARE StatChangeTrigger ENTRIES, never RequiredStatValues. Gate 1, hw_switch_aurora {1,1}: DEPARTURE FROM THE DECISION, which lists only the next two gates: every Harsh Wilds STA carries exactly one hw_switch_ entry (the [gate-switch] rule of HarshWilds-Events.Tests.ps1, the same rule that gives Tgr_HW_PlagueSwarm its switch), and it makes 'inert at its switch 0' true for an aurora already running when the config is turned off: with the switch at 0 the mood step stops at once, and only the alert lingers until the timer ends. Gate 2, vanilla IsNightUnderOpenSky (b2d185dbbb6aa0f46905c6700faebe12) {1,1}: outside under an open sky between 17:00 and 07:00; it turns 0 the instant the player steps indoors and at dawn. Gate 3, hw_stat_aurora {1,40} (1 to HW_AURORA_TICKS, the timer's whole running range): an aurora is running. THE STEP: HW_AURORA_MORALE_PER_TICK = +0.5 with IgnoreNovelty true. Morale UsesNovelty is true and an STA's stat write carries an action name, so without IgnoreNovelty a repeated write would be staled to nothing (.decomp/GameManager.cs ChangeStat, events_sky.md section 5). An STA write is a PERMANENT base write (Permanent, clamped into Morale's -350 to 350) and Morale's own BaseRatePerTick is 0, so nothing but the game's mood rates ever takes it back; that is safe here for three reasons, all MEASURED from the export on 2026-09-30 and enforced by the [aurora-mood] rule of HarshWilds-Events.Tests.ps1. (1) It is bounded: at most 40 armed ticks, so at most +20 for one aurora (+0.5 x 40), and the roll needs the timer at 0 and a 96 tick cooldown. (2) It cannot reach a cap or an edge worth naming: vanilla Morale's Content band {100,250} carries a Morale RATE of -1 (Happy {251,325} -2, Euphoric {326,350} -3), so at 100 and above the step is out-weighed (+0.5 - 1 is a net fall), and Morale cannot be lifted past about 100.5 by this file from any start; it never approaches Happy, Euphoric or the cap of 350, so it can never land exactly ON the cap (the CLAUDE.md Perks clamp trap: a starting modifier is clamped onto the cap, which is the top of a trigger band). Below -100 the vanilla bands already recover Morale by +0.5 to +2 a tick and this only adds to that. Between -99 and 99 vanilla has no band, so Morale rests where the step leaves it, like any one-shot mood item. (3) No SelfTriggeredAction watches Morale: read all 95 vanilla STAs (the GUID map count and the export folder agree at 95) by GUID and by name, none names Morale or Light in a StatChangeTrigger, RequiredStatValues or write (the same scan found both consumers of MoonShape, Tgr_Apparitions and Tgr_MoonMaidenDream, so it can see a consumer), and no STA folder of any mod in this repo names Morale either; the only other vanilla files naming Morale are GameStat statuses and CardData, CharacterPerk and Encounter rows, which apply their own rates and effects (Content's own effects are ImmuneSystem +50 and a Derealization rate, reversed when Morale falls back below 100). One accepted side effect of any small positive mood source: a player already near 99 flickers around the Content edge and the Content status can re-alert as it toggles (a Copper Necklace's +0.25 does the same); harness probe P3. Every number here is a TUNABLE PLACEHOLDER, session-inferred and unmeasured against play, never balanced. It drops no card and needs no player text.
